question: arXiv:2209.00006v2 compares the best-fit spectra of its Galactic Center excess candidates when each is fitted together with ring-based templates. Which candidate gives the faintest excess, and how good is its fit? What does the paper say about the spectra of the candidates that include the boxy bulge? And how does the dark matter spectrum obtained with the ring-based templates compare with those spectra and with the dark matter result obtained with the astrophysics-based templates of Cholis et al.?

arguments.answer: The faintest excess with the ring-based templates is the X-shaped bulge, and it also gives the worst fit to the data of all the candidates. I did not look up its table values. The candidates that include the boxy bulge (boxy bulge alone, boxy bulge plus the nuclear stellar bulge, and boxy bulge together with the X-shaped bulge) all have very similar spectra. These spectra are relatively soft, which the paper says is compatible with the excess having absorbed unmodeled diffuse flux. The dark matter spectrum fitted with the ring-based templates is harder on average than those boxy-bulge spectra. It is similar in shape to the dark matter spectrum from the astrophysics-based templates of Cholis et al., but lower in flux. It also shows "wiggles" between energy bins that neither dark matter annihilation nor millisecond pulsars predict.
